reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents Forsage as a make-money system and demonstrates joining through upline and downline links, activating levels, and claims that amounts return to a wallet or account when more people join. The speaker points to a displayed account balance and claims of earnings, alongside referral and activation controls, as support for participation.

opening.argument: Judge, the title asks whether Forsage is working; it does not promise that every viewer will earn money. The description urges viewers to watch the full explanation before drawing conclusions. And the speaker says viewers can inspect an ID themselves. Those are reasons to read the earnings figures as claims being explained and checked, not as a guaranteed return offered to the audience.

citations.quote: Forsage working ?
Watch the full video without skipping any parts - Otherwise, you won't understand it well
So you guys can also open any of your ID

rebuttal.rebuttal: The other side quotes conditional descriptions: money follows a person joining, and later amounts follow further joins and level activation. That establishes what the speaker says the system does, but it does not establish that the displayed earnings are attainable for a viewer, or that the speaker guarantees they will be. The question in the title leaves that issue open.

citations.quote: when you will join a person then you will get the access load money will come directly from other person after joining
Forsage working ?

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A question mark and an invitation to watch are not risk warnings. The title also advertises earning and making money, while the speaker tells viewers that adding people and activating levels will send amounts back to a wallet. The absence of an explicit guarantee does not undo that instructional earnings pitch.

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker frames this as an explanation of a visible account: viewers are told they can open an ID and check its figures, and the speaker moves on to show their own account ID. Explaining the X3 and X4 panels, including how entries recycle, can be an operational demonstration even when the subject is an earning system. The cited account walkthrough does not by itself show a viewer signing up or paying.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The other side correctly identifies the upline/downline and level-buying explanation. But explaining those terms is also necessary to make sense of the account the speaker is showing. Its quotes describe the mechanism; they do not show that a viewer actually joined or bought a level. The speaker explicitly offers account inspection as part of the presentation.

citations.quote: upliner means the link from which you are join and downliner means the link from which that person join
So you guys can also open any of your ID

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A demonstration can still instruct viewers in participation. Here the speaker describes what happens when 'you' join a person, activate the next level, and add another person so money returns to 'your wallet.' Those are actionable earning instructions, not merely an explanation of historical account figures.

citations.quote: when you will join a person then you will get the access load money will come directly from other person after joining
if you want you can activate the second level similarly you can add this second level person then it will be re-recycled and will come back in your wallet

opening.argument: Judge, the interface shown here has priced levels and an activation control; the speaker describes buying levels and inspecting account information. Referral relationships are visible, but those observations alone do not prove that a displayed balance was paid out, that returns are guaranteed, or that a viewer must surrender credentials. On this record, the narrower reading is a presentation of a referral-style promotion and its purchase options, without treating the service as verified or safe.

citations.quote: You can buy from 100, 400, 200, and even if you come down the line, I give you 2 and 2

rebuttal.rebuttal: The other side points to links, levels and money moving after joins. Those are serious features, but its quoted narration does not establish a guaranteed profit or a completed payout to the viewer. The speaker also describes levels as things one can choose to buy. The distinction matters when judging what this particular video proves, rather than assuming every displayed account figure is withdrawable income.

citations.quote: upliner means the link from which you are join and downliner means the link from which that person join

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing guarantee and payout proof do not remove the mechanism the speaker describes. This is not just a priced purchase with incidental referrals: the speaker says money comes from another person joining, explains upline/downline links, and says additional joins and level purchases return amounts to the participant's account.
